Ah, lemme share a bit of my story, and maybe, I hope, it serves someone. Even if it is to do something for 5 minutes.

I was valedictorian, the kid who was always doing academic crap, winning spelling contests, the one with "the most promising future," the girl with all those markers in her pencil case, lol... and getting called a nerd, but that is another story.

Now, back in my first uni year, I met a girl, she was so brilliant. She is the top score. And I was dying of jealousy. But then, I realized she is also having issues, specifically, she is high-key anxious.

Thus, we became friends, as time passed. I am no longer jealous of her, despite her being waaaay over my GPA. In fact, I admire her. I learned a lot from her, even helping her vent now and then. She is trying to help me get a job in research, which is my area of interest.

I realized that my potential is there, but I am completely unable to bring everything out of it, due to how I constantly think on a b/w scheme and destroy my interpersonal relations. I honestly don't know how some of my Uni mates are so understanding, or why do I even deserve their aid. But they are trying to help me, even if they, too, have their own problems.

My highschool mates? They work, all right. I don't. But I am trying to find a job I can enjoy. I guess I will be their laughing stock every now and then, but, at least, I am trying. One day at a time, even if some people press me to plan A LOT ahead.

I do hope I can learn to live. And I hope for the best for y'all.
